details: PLAUSIBLE: the harness relays the owner's own words verbatim; none of the 17 real harness lines holds "Report:", and
the owner writes short replies, so it is rare. The brief chose "the first user entry that carries a Report: label";
taking the last labelled leading user entry meets the brief's cases too and puts the computed task (always after the

failing_case: Workflow transcript: line 1 "[Workflow harness — user request] ... \n  посмотри Report: /x/old-check.json", line 2
"[Workflow harness — computed task] ... Report: `/x/check-new.json`." first_entry returns line 1 (first labelled
entry), so the hook reads /x/old-check.json: most often "cannot be read" or "older than the checker's start" (no mark,
the bug this change fixes, back), at worst another checker's newer data. It should read /x/check-new.json.
fix_hint: Keep scanning the leading user entries and return the last one with a label (labelled = (text, start) and continue;
return labelled or first after the loop).
pass_cases: 1. Harness line with a Report: label, then the check prompt with its own label -> the mark from the prompt's label.
2. K13 (harness with no label, then the prompt) -> the mark.
3. K13b (no label in any leading entry) -> no mark, "no Report: line".
findings.summary: a Report: in the owner's relayed request wins over the computed task's label

notes: Fine: the loop stops at the first assistant entry; attachment entries (no message) after the prompt are skipped; an

hook that read past the assistant entry would report "cannot be read" for rep.json, not "no Report: line").

No waste added: the hook reads at most the leading entries; no extra run or step.
